To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have fabricated a sub-500-nm resonant interband-tunneling-diode (RIT) with a peak current density of 1 kA/cm2 and a peak-to-valley current ratio of 2.4 at 77 K, without using any fine line lithography, by combining epitaxial regrowth of a thin InAs/AlAsSb/GaAsSb heterostructure on patterned substratesthat is, a sidewall spacer defined device.
the device is a resonant interband tunnelling diode that has a current density of 2.5 kA/cm 2 and a differential negative resistance of 2 V/μm 2.

we have developed a novel fabrication technique for RITDs that does not require fine-line lithography and that we have fabricated and characterized the first RITDs that are fully defined by sidewall spacers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of resonant tunneling diodes (RTDs) in the InAs/Al _{x} Ga _{1–x} Sb/GaSb system.
the development of novel semiconductor devices based on resonant interband transitions.

the fabrication and characterization of a novel resonant interband tunnelling diode (RITT) structure, in which the tunnel barrier is formed at the heterointerface of an InAs/Al _{x} Ga _{1-x} Sb superlattice (SL).
